gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the inverter's own idle draw counts as daily load: BLUETTI lists the Apex 300's idle loss at 20 W, which is 0.48 kWh/day (20 W × 24 h), or 22% of the 2.2 kWh/day that ChatGPT's own sizing assumed for a weekend cabin, before a single light is on.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and cited no rival pages in either saved chat, so the only comparison is its own answer. It sized arrays and batteries from appliance use (2.2 kWh/day, 1.0 kW array, 5 kWh battery at 3 sun-hours, 80% efficiency, 1.5 days of autonomy). It never counts the inverter's standby draw, and it names no product (its 'Shop' cards were blank). It does mention 'battery temperature protection', so cold-weather charging is partly covered, but idle draw is not. It scores 2, not 3, because I couldn't confirm the component kit's own inverter idle figure from a page I opened. That figure is what would make this fact decide between a power-station set and a 48 V component kit.
kit_items: Panels: Sun Gold Power SGM-5K5E's 6 × 200 W mono panels (1,200 W) or BLUETTI's 2 × 500 W bundle (1,000 W). Either meets the 1.0 kW array ChatGPT suggested; the single 500 W panel in the Apex 300 + 500W bundle does not.

Inverter + MPPT: Sun Gold Power's 5,000 W 48 V 120 V Wi-Fi inverter in the SGM-5K5E (one box, which covers ChatGPT's 'inverter and compatible MPPT' line), or the BLUETTI Apex 300 all-in-one (3,840 W, 120/240 V, 20 W idle loss).
Battery: one 51.2 V 100 Ah LiFePO4 (5.12 kWh) in the SGM-5K5E, which matches ChatGPT's '48V-class 100Ah, about 5 kWh' example. The Apex 300 has 2,764.8 Wh built in and expands with B300K/B500K packs.

Protection and wiring: the SGM-5K5E includes a 160 A DC breaker, a 25 A PV breaker, a 4 AWG breaker-to-inverter cable, one 50 ft PV extension set and 6 sets of Z-brackets. It has no AC disconnect, grounding kit or combiner, so the buyer still adds those.

Cold weather: Sun Gold Power sells a self-heating SGH48100T battery only in its 'T' variants of the larger 10 kW and 20 kW kits. The SGM-5K5E listing names a plain 100 Ah 51.2 V LiFePO4 battery, so a cabin left unheated in winter needs that swap or a heated battery room.
